style: retail swing/position trader, growth-stock fundamentals plus chart timing
edge_principles: Screen the universe on fundamentals (EPS and revenue growth, return on equity) and use the chart only for timing
Decide the exit (fixed max loss of about 8-10%) and an expected profit target before entering; place the stop immediately
Once price reaches the expected target, tighten the stop sharply so a winner cannot become a loser
Trade with the broad index trend; most stocks follow the market direction
Specialise in a handful of names to learn their recurring intraday and range behaviour
Review every trade on the chart, winners as well as losers
notes: Career/journey interview; mostly general swing-trading process. One loosely specified fundamental-filter swing approach and an anecdotal range trade, no precise intraday rules.

edge_principles: Implied volatility tends to overstate realized moves; be a net seller of options premium
Act like a casino: many small, independent, high-probability bets rather than few large ones
Risk 1-5% of the account per position; a cited tastytrade study showed the same 75% win-rate strategy losing half the account at 50% allocation versus gaining at 5%
Liquidity first: only trade stocks with >1M shares/day and tight option spreads, otherwise the edge is lost in the bid-ask
Check portfolio-level directional balance (net delta) before adding a trade; skip good setups that make the book lopsided
Diversify across expiries and strategies, not just underlyings
Commit to a fixed rule set for ~a year / 100+ trades before judging a high-win-rate strategy
Roll losing short-premium positions out in time for a credit instead of closing
notes: Options-selling philosophy interview; describes short strangles/iron condors in general terms with no precise strike/DTE rules, so no concrete stock setup extracted.

style: retail penny-stock momentum and short seller
edge_principles: Choose a niche with weak competition (low-priced stocks large funds ignore)
Only trade the hottest movers of the day; ignore stocks that are not moving
Cut losses very quickly; one large loss is what ruins small-cap traders
Take the 'meat' of a move (10-30%) rather than trying to catch the top or bottom
After a losing streak, trade smaller, paper trade or stop - do not size up to win it back
notes: Introduces his pump-and-dump short thesis at a high level; no precise trigger, so the single setup is low confidence.

style: systematic end-of-day trend follower and short-term mean reversion (The Chartist)
edge_principles: Know why the strategy makes money so you can tell a regime mismatch from a broken system
Trend following wins ~50% with 3:1 payoffs; accept long flat periods (e.g. 24% in one quarter, nothing for 8 months)
Diversify by adding uncorrelated strategies (trend breakout + short mean reversion) rather than switching after a drawdown
Commissions and small account size can require 20-40%/yr just to break even; size capital to the trade frequency
Measure realized slippage per trade; an illiquid-market strategy lost 11-15%/yr to about $45 slippage per trade
Fixed-fractional sizing: a 10% stock stop equals ~0.5-0.8% of capital when held in a portfolio
Automate end-of-day order generation; no intraday watching
notes: Systematic process interview. Two strategies described at a structural level (ASX small-cap momentum breakout, S&P 500 3-day mean reversion) without exact parameters.

style: retail trend follower / swing trader (New Trader U)
edge_principles: Risk at most 1% of capital per trade and at most ~3% total open risk across positions
Size positions by the instrument's daily range so a full adverse day costs no more than the 1% budget
Use end-of-day (closing) stops when position size is small enough to tolerate intraday noise
Avoid deep drawdowns: a 50% loss needs 100% to recover
Accumulate enough capital before trading actively (he suggests $25-30k) so costs do not dominate
React to price; do not predict
notes: Mostly risk-management and mindset. Gives three concrete daily-chart rules: RSI swing in an uptrend, range breakout to all-time highs with MA trailing stop, and index 200-day reclaim.

style: retail Gann-based swing trader, daily charts
edge_principles: Establish the bigger trend on weekly/monthly charts first; take mainly longs in bull phases and shorts in bear phases
Avoid trading signals in sideways/choppy markets; most whipsaw comes from ignoring regime
Split the position: take half at a high-probability target, hold the other half for an extended move
Add on fresh signals in the trend rather than all at once
Review past trades on the chart; one subscriber found all profits came from three setups in three markets - cut everything else
Specialise in 2-3 markets and no more than two concurrent trades
Range-vs-volume reading: a narrowing range on equal volume signals more supply entering
Treat widely publicised bullish/bearish news near extremes as a contrary signal
notes: Gann-style swing trading on daily charts. Main setup is the 50% retracement coinciding with a double/triple bottom, confirmed by a swing-chart signal.

style: ex-prop tape reader; equity and options (weeklies) day/swing trader
edge_principles: Edge for a discretionary human is reading the tape (Level 2 + time and sales) for large-player accumulation footprints
Never trade in front of a news release; wait for the algorithmic reaction to finish and trade after
Scale out into strength (sell into the move) rather than waiting to exit the whole size at the top - liquidity vanishes at the turn
Swing trading one or two names and waiting for the big move was his most consistent mode; constant day trading led to overtrading
Trading to cover rent or recover losses produces forced trades; stand aside on no-opportunity days
After a run of losses, size down for weeks until a few winners restore confidence
Large size in options is visible to market makers; vary execution and order routing
notes: Mostly career and psychology. His method is discretionary tape reading of accumulation before breakouts, with no measurable rules; one high-discretion setup recorded.

style: hedge fund operator (SangLucci Capital), options premium seller, HFT/market-structure
edge_principles: Measure P&L per share/contract; many break-even hand traders are simply losing the spread they cross - passive (limit) entries can flip them to profitable
Order-flow routing matters: sold/internalised flow gets picked off in fast markets; route directly or use smarter execution
He cites that well under a third (~28%) of intraday breakout attempts succeed; markets chop more than they trend intraday, so be selective with breakouts
Set stops according to the participant timeframe you are trading (swing positions should not carry day-trader-tight stops)
Know your regime: scale up in conditions that suit your style (he sells premium in choppy markets, scales back in breakout markets)
Write entries/exits as explicit if-then pseudocode so entry and exit signals are consistent
Discretionary size does not scale linearly; increase size gradually with emotional tolerance
notes: Market-structure and career interview. No concrete setup; key quantitative claim is that most intraday breakouts fail and spread-crossing explains much of retail break-even P&L.

style: retail small-cap momentum trader, mainly short seller of overextended runners
markets: US OTC and NASDAQ small caps
edge_principles: Use a broker whose execution fits the strategy; slow fills turn a planned small stop into a large loss
Trade only liquid, volatile names (he wants >= ~$5M traded on the day for listed stocks)
Narrow to one or two setups, track each in a spreadsheet (returns, frequency) before sizing up
Trade the ticker, not the company: ignore fundamental bias when price breaks your level
Place stops at chart levels, then size the position so the distance to that level fits the dollar risk
Never average up into a short that breaks to new highs of the run; a $290k loss came from holding and adding
Hiding the open P&L column reduced emotional exits
notes: Small-cap specialist; two daily-chart setups (fading multi-day spikes in listed small caps, buying breakouts to new highs of an OTC promotion) plus buying newly announced promotions (not testable).

style: independent intraday equities trader, VWAP-based, moving to systematic
edge_principles: Use VWAP as the day's honest average price and primary bias filter; it is fast early, slows midday, picks up slightly near the close
Prefer liquid, 'boring' large caps over in-play news names; a 45-cent move in a mega cap is enough
Decide direction first, then location; if odds are strongly one way, enter with partial size instead of waiting for a perfect entry
A setup is only worth trading if it shows positive expectancy across hundreds of stocks, not a few charts
Think in expectancy = payoff x probability, including sizing, partial exits and stop handling - not raw risk:reward
Master one approach deeply before adding others
Keep stakes small early; mental burnout ends more careers than blown accounts
His busiest/most important window is 10:00-12:00 ET
notes: Two-hour VWAP philosophy interview with little precise rule detail; one loosely specified VWAP bias setup recorded.

style: retail futures day trader, market/volume profile and price action (Optic Trading)
edge_principles: Top-down: mark key reference zones on monthly, weekly, daily then 5-min charts before the open
Trade value (where volume accumulates in the profile), not just price; migrating value signals direction
Within a balance area, trade from extremes; the middle is chop
Rest limit orders at pre-planned levels and let the market come to you
Expect 3-5 years to consistency; stay on simulation until profitable there
Add a new market via historical replay, then sim alongside live markets, then small live size
After a stop-out, never double size to win it back (revenge trading caused his largest loss)
notes: Profile-based futures day trader with 11 setups; describes one in detail, the balance-area breakout failure.
